questions.question: Concretely, what does a gate look like when you write it—is it a test script, a threshold number in a config file, or something a human still has to read?
questions.why: The talk keeps saying 'gate' as if it's obvious but never shows the actual file or check.

questions.question: When a usage limit killed three build lanes mid-work, how did you recover those lanes the next morning—rerun from scratch or resume from the last commit?
questions.why: The speaker mentions the kill on September 7th but not what recovery actually involved.

questions.question: What does 'reviewer one tier up' mean in practice—are you literally pointing a bigger model at a smaller model's diff, and how is that wired up?
questions.why: He names the rule but never shows the mechanism for picking or invoking the reviewer model.

questions.question: For the overnight caps—8 calls, 60 seconds, $6—where do you actually set those, and what stops an agent from just retrying past them?
questions.why: He gives the numbers but not where they live or how they're enforced without a platform team.

questions.question: The idle tab burned a full day's allowance before the watchdog caught it—what is the watchdog, and how would I build one for my own overnight runs?
questions.why: He flags the failure and says 'the watchdog came after' but never describes it.

questions.question: If I've never used a worktree before, what's the actual command sequence to spin up a lane, and how does it merge back when the gate passes?
questions.why: He assumes worktrees are familiar, but as someone who's only used git branches this is the part I'd get stuck on.

questions.question: You used 'top-3' and 'embedding' without defining them on screen—can you walk through what a top-3 check is actually computing?
questions.why: Several slides lean on top-3 and embedding scores as if they're self-explanatory to a first-time viewer.

questions.question: For the persona review gate, who or what actually plays the four personas and returns DONE or NOT—is that a scripted prompt, and how do I stop it from rubber-stamping?
questions.why: The panel said DONE while the real app was 'pretty much unusable,' so the mechanism behind the verdict matters.

questions.question: In the starter kit, which file would I open first if I just want to copy the gate-and-flag pattern for my own overnight runs?
questions.why: He points to starter/ at the end but gives no entry point for someone trying this next week.

questions.question: How many lanes can realistically run in parallel before the coordinator session itself becomes the bottleneck?
questions.why: The chart shows this talk's own lanes but never states a practical ceiling for parallelism.
